newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher for third straight day.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher for third straight day.

text.p: The won ended higher against the U.S. unit for the third consecutive day on Thursday, supported by active dollar-selling intervention by the central Bank of Korea (BOK), traders said.
There was no impact seen from the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, they added.

The won ended at 854.90, against Wednesday's close of 859.00. It opened at 858.00, and moved between 853.50 and 859.00. "These days it's very difficult to predict how the dollar will move, because the current level is artificially induced by the BOK's intervention," said a local bank dealer.
Traders said the central bank sold dollars on the spot market and in three-month and six-month forward trading.
The central bank has refused to confirm or deny talk of its intervention in the interbank market.
"The central bank actively intervened, but the market doesn't want to sell dollars at this level," said a European bank dealer.
"Players are cautious of building short dollar positions because they fear the greenback will turn bullish again."
The won is being pressured by a widening trade deficit and the dollar's strength on world markets.
The local dealer predicted a won/dollar range of 853-858 on Friday, while the European dealer put it at 855-860.
The base mid-rate for Friday was pegged at 855.50, against 859.30 on Thursday.
